program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm description; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: RC5-32/r/b (r = 0 to 16 rounds, keys of 1 to 16 bytes) in CBC mode: 29 of 29 ciphertexts of the RFC 2040 test vectors match, including 2 of 2 with RC5-CBC-Pad padding

expected_values_source.what: section 9.3 "Test results" of RFC 2040 (R. Baldwin and R. Rivest, "The RC5, RC5-CBC, RC5-CBC-Pad, and RC5-CTS Algorithms", 1996), 29 test results; the constants P32 and Q32 are from its section on magic constants
expected_values_source.note: the vectors come from the RFC, not from Rivest's 1994 paper (whose own five printed vectors were not fetched). Data copied as numbers; the RFC's test program was not copied

negative_control: built with RC5_P32=0xb7e15162 (last bit of P32 changed), 0 of 29 vectors match and the program exits 1
not_checked: word sizes other than 32 bits (the RFC vectors use 32 only)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces the RFC 2040 RC5 ciphertexts for 29 inputs. It does not show RC5 is secure.
